title.en: The writer, the novel and the young doctor

hook.en: A young doctor, tired and unsure of himself, is called out at midnight. By dawn he will have fought for two lives, and learnt what being a doctor really means.

objectives.en: Describe Andrew Manson and the setting

narration.en: A young doctor, tired and unsure of himself, is called out at midnight. By dawn he will have fought for two lives, and learnt what being a doctor really means.

body.en: A.J. Cronin (1896–1981) was a Scottish doctor who became a famous novelist. "Birth" is an episode from his novel "The Citadel" (1937), which follows the career of a young doctor and criticises the medical practices of his time. Cronin's own medical experience gives the episode its realism.

Let us map everyone involved in this night, with the doctor at the centre.

say.en: At the centre is Andrew Manson, a young doctor in his first post.
Joe Morgan, a miner, waits anxiously for his first child.
Susan Morgan, his wife, faces a long and difficult labour.
Susan's elderly mother watches over her.
A midwife helps at the delivery.
All this happens in Blaenelly, a mining town in Wales.

body.en: Andrew Manson is a newly qualified doctor working in Blaenelly, a mining town in Wales. Joe Morgan, a miner, and his wife Susan are expecting their first child after nearly twenty years of marriage. Susan's elderly mother and a midwife are also present.
